articles.text: Special agent Armstrong telegraphed Tuesday from Fort Reno, that there was no danger of trouble arising at the Arapahoe and Cheyenne agencies.
articles.summary: Special agent Armstrong reported no danger of trouble at the Arapahoe and Cheyenne agencies.

articles.text: There are 96,596,480 acres of land in Dakota, 55,297,180 of which are unsurveyed. In total area, Montana comes next with 92,016,640 acres, then come New Mexico, Arizona, Nevada, Colorado and Wyoming in the order named, the latter having a total area of 62,645,120 acres.
articles.summary: Land-area figures for Dakota and other western territories.

articles.text: There have been 42,667 timber-culture entries in Dakota, including 8,246,304 acres. Nebraska comes next with 25,031 entries and an acreage of 3,553,479. As this calls for the raising and growth of about 515,418 acres of trees in Dakota, future generations may well thank the foresight of our government in making the timber-culture law although its provisions are greatly abused.
articles.summary: Timber-culture entries in Dakota and praise for the timber-culture law.

articles.text: The Pall Mall Ga[z]ette, of London, has been exposing the vices of the nobility in such a way that it is seriously arousing public opinion. It has long been an open secret in England that the common people have no rights that the nobility consider themselves bound to respect. The Gazette is the first champion the people have ever had that has done them any good. It is doing a good work and has the support of the large mass of the English people. Rev. Spurgeon, as well as many other ministers, are giving enthusiastic sanction to the Gazette.
articles.summary: Comment on the Pall Mall Gazette's exposure of the vices of the English nobility.

articles.text: In the course of time, a vast amount of land in Dakota which now is unproductive, can be made as valuable as any with artesian wells. Especially between Medora and the Black Hills there is a large extent of country that is valueless for agriculture and only moderately valuable for stock, owing to the scarcity or total lack of water. There is plenty of land at present nearer the railroad and better watered, but the time is coming when this land will all be readily salable and the ones who establish successful artesian wells will reap a rich profit.
articles.summary: Packard predicts artesian wells will make dry land between Medora and the Black Hills valuable.

articles.text: We are indebted to a pamphlet entitled "Range and ranch cattle business of the United States" by Joseph Nimmo, Jr., Chief of the Bureau of Statistics, for many of the figures in this week's issue. The pamphlet covers a great deal of ground, giving many interesting facts relative to the cattle industry and dealing especially with the bearings of the cattle business upon the internal and foreign commerce of the United States. It gives a complete history of the range cattle and dressed beef industries of the United States and is in the main correct. The article on Dakota is however, not only misleading but almost entirely wrong. The facts(?) were furnished by a man who is personally entirely ignorant of the cattle business. With this and a few other exceptions the pamphlet is the most valuable one on range cattle ever published.
articles.summary: Packard credits Joseph Nimmo Jr.'s range-cattle report for the week's figures but calls its Dakota article almost entirely wrong.

articles.text: Trouble has at last begun between the trail men and the Kansas cattle men. J. R. Blocker, Pugsley Bros., N. Dowling, H. S. Holly, J. W. Driskill, J. T. Lytle, M. C. Campbell and others have been arrested by deputy U. S. Marshal Bell and taken to Dodge City, Kansas. These men have over 50,000 head of cattle on the trail, which are now stopped south of the Canadian river. Their preliminary trial has probably already occurred. It is likely that every means will be used to avoid the trial as, it being a test case, thousands and probably hundreds of thousands of dollars will be spent before its decision. At any rate the arrests show that the Kansans are thoroughly in earnest about the enforcement of the quarantine laws. The decision will materially affect cattle interests, especially those of the south and will be looked forward to with intense interest.
articles.summary: Texas trail drivers arrested under Kansas quarantine laws and taken to Dodge City.

articles.headline: Northwestern Stock Business.
articles.text:
For the benefit of those of our readers who have not a personal knowledge of the history of stock raising in the northwest, a short account may be agreeable.

In 1864, or rather early in 1865 it was learned that cattle would fatten in the north better than in the south. A government trader was overtaken by a hard snow storm on the Laramie plains and turned his oxen out, as he supposed to die. Early in the spring, however, he found them in even better condition than when turned out. This, taken in connection with the fact that buffalo lived and grew exceedingly fat in Dakota, Montana and Wyoming, first drew the attention of cattlemen to the northwest as a beef coutry.

Capitalists soon took advantage of the opportunities offered and began driving cattle from the southern ranges to grow into beef. This has been kept up to the present time and it is fair to presume that within five years the northern ranges will be as full as is safe, taking into consideration the natural increase of the herds.

The range territory includes the principal part of the Indian territory, the western parts of Kansas, Nebraska and Dakota, nearly all of Montana, Idaho, Wyoming, Utah, Arizona, New Mexico, Colorado, Nevada and portions of California, Oregon and Washington. This area includes over 1,160,000 square miles.

A fair illustration of the marvelous growth of the cattle industry is shown by the growth of the Montana and Wyoming associations. Two years ago, according to President Bryan, the Montana association consisted of seven members. Now there are over a hundred and fifty members. In 1873 the Wyoming association consisted of ten members, owning about 20,000 cattle, valued at $350,000. In 1885 the Wyoming association has 435 members, owning 2,000,000 head of cattle and valued at $100,000,000.

The cattle business of the west and northwest differs somewhat from the way it is conducted in the south. In Texas, the most of the land is owned by the cattlemen themselves. In the Indian territory the land is for the most part leased, but in Wyoming, Montana and Dakota, the vast majority of the cattle are grazing on government land. In these territories, this will doubtless be the case for some time to come, as the cattle country is in the dry area and agriculture cannot be carried on except by irrigation. It will be many years before the land not requiring irrigation will be taken up and the time is especially far distant when it will pay to irrigate lands far from railroads in this western country. The grass receives an abundance of moisture from the snows and spring rains, the dry weather comes on early and cures the grass standing. It is then equal to cut timothy.

Only a few years ago the Indians held almost undisputed control of what is now the range cattle country of the west and northwest. After the Custer massacre the government adopted stringent measures with reference to compelling the Indians to stay on their reservations, thus practically opening the country to the stock interests. There is now no farther danger in the cattle country from Indian outbreaks as the cow-boys could easily quell any disturbance.

The cattle business is now as firmly established and the profits can be as easily calculated as in other pursuits, the results of which are not absolutely certain. There is always a market for beef and stock cattle. Prices vary a little but have steadily increased from the $3 to $4 Texas steer of twenty-five years ago, to the $50 to $60 Montana steer of to-day.

The work is now reduced to a system and everyone is compelled to act honestly by his neighbor. Ten years ago a man might draw to a branding iron and get a herd. Now he would as surely get a rope or states prison. From the thorough detective and inspection system of the stock associations, it is almost impossible to act dishonestly. A man's cattle when branded, are as safe a hundred miles from his ranch as they are at home. The unwritten law of the range is "treat your neighbor white and he'll treat you w[hit]e."
articles.summary: Packard's history and survey of the northwestern range-cattle business, from the 1864-65 discovery that cattle wintered on the northern plains to the stock associations of 1885.

articles.text: Of the slaughtering-houses in Chicago Swift Bros. & Co., did the largest business, killing 401,617 cattle. Armour & Co. came next with 306,374.
articles.summary: Swift and Armour slaughter figures at Chicago.

articles.text: There were 98,000 cattle shipped west over the Northern Pacific last year according to the statement of General freight agent Hannaford. They were mostly she stock, one's and two's.
articles.summary: 98,000 cattle were shipped west over the Northern Pacific last year, per freight agent Hannaford.

articles.text: In Wyoming there are fifty-six varieties of natural grasses. As the soil, physical characteristics and climate of Dakota are about the same as Wyoming, there are probably the same number in this territory. In addition, alfalfa and several other artificial grasses have been tried and we have not yet heard of any failures in this direction.
articles.summary: Dakota probably has as many native grasses as Wyoming's fifty-six; alfalfa has been tried successfully.

articles.text: The largest number of cattle received during any one month last year at the Chicago yards was 198,717 in October. The lowest number was in March, 122,633. The large receipts during the latter month as well as in the winter and early spring is probably due to the fact that farmers are making a general practice of raising feeders for a high market.
articles.summary: Monthly Chicago cattle receipts for last year.

articles.text: The total value of the live cattle and beef products exported from the United States during the year ending June 30, 1884 was $41,080,001. Of this total, Great Britain and Ireland took more than three-quarters. There has been a steady and rapid increase in this export business since 1875, the total value of shipments during that year being $11,728,358.
articles.summary: Value of U.S. live cattle and beef exports.

articles.text: All live cattle shipped from the United States to England, must be killed at the port of entry within five days of their arrival and cannot be taken into the interior. This is a distinction made against our cattle by England, without any just cause. The dressed beef industry of the United States makes it far more profitable to ship beef in that way, but as a matter of principle, the government should have England's restriction on our cattle removed or give her a taste of how a similar restriction on our part would seem. Cattle shipped from Canada to England are subject to no restrictions whatever.
articles.summary: Packard protests England's restriction on live American cattle.

articles.summary: Mrs. Foraier has photographed the Bad Lands.

articles.summary: Puff for John Munro's cigars.

articles.text: The Elk is still the favorite place in Little Missouri to "moisten." All can be sure of good goods and good treatment.
articles.summary: Puff for the Elk saloon in Little Missouri.

articles.summary: Aleck Connell bought an outfit and plans a Bad Lands cattle ranch.

articles.text: Beginning with to-day, money orders, both domestic and foreign, will be sold at the Medora office. This will be a great convenience and save much time and trouble in paying outside bills.

articles.text: "When you smell something good about the city make up your mind somebody is smoking one of Munro's El Mapa Mundi Cigars."
articles.summary: Puff for Munro's cigars.

articles.text: Dr. Duncan, of Glendive, was here Sunday. He put a plaster-of-paris splint on Joe. McCoul's leg which enables him to move about and will hasten his complete recovery.
articles.summary: Dr. Duncan of Glendive splinted Joe McCoul's leg.

articles.text: Rassie Deffebach returned from Dickinson Tuesday night. His family is comfortably quartered there and Rassie will make it his home. He will be at the Bad Lands cattle Co's. ranch and handle that outfit.
articles.summary: Rassie Deffebach has settled his family in Dickinson and will run the Bad Lands Cattle Co. ranch.

articles.text: Dr. H. W. Coe, of Mandan, our member of the legislature, was here Monday closing up Coll McClellan's census work. Dr. Coe was the recipient of a gold headed cane at Valley City recently, from his granger constituents there.
articles.summary: Legislator Dr. H. W. Coe visited Medora to close up the census work.

articles.text:
"I would advise you to go
Over to John Munro,
And get a cigar,
That beats everything by far,
El Mapa Mundi its called
It snatches them all bald."

(We wish it distinctly understood that we are only responsible for the sentiment of the above. All the credit of the rhyme and rhythm is to be given to Ed. Goodkind, of Bismarck.—Ed.)
articles.summary: Comic verse puffing Munro's cigars, credited to Ed. Goodkind of Bismarck.

articles.text: The Marquise, Wm. Van Driesche and hunting party consisting of Vic and Frank Smith, Tom Skinner and Sweet start this evening for Huntley, Mont. The horses have already been shipped there, this being the starting-point for the overland journey to the Big Horn. The party will be gone about a month.
articles.summary: The Marquise de Morès and a hunting party leave for Huntley, Mont., to start for the Big Horn.

articles.text: A. R. Kelsey, manager of the Glendive branch of J. S. Collins & Co., called at the Cow Boy office this morning. He reports a first-rate trade for his house, but as the most of it is in and west of Miles City, the branch will be removed there on or about August 10. The firm is now building a brick store room for their accommodation in Miles.
articles.summary: J. S. Collins & Co.'s Glendive branch will move to Miles City about August 10.

articles.text: Experience is the only teacher in regard to the way beef will dress out. There was every prospect that range cattle would be in condition fully two or three weeks earlier than last year. The grass was fully that much earlier and larger in proportion than last year. It is doubtful though, if the beef is any earlier. The grass has grown to quantity and not to quality. Considerable good beef has been slaughtered here, but it has not come up to the high standard expected of it. It is doubtful if any first-class beef will be killed before August 1.
articles.summary: Range beef is not up to standard; first-class beef unlikely before August 1.

articles.text: Prairie fires are again forcing themselves into notice and it is time that stockmen took immediate steps to protect themselves. A large portion of the country south of Belfield has been burned over and yesterday one was burning in the Bad Lands near Sully Springs. No effort has yet been made to make fire guards either by individuals or the railroad company. This is a short-sighted policy. A week of such weather as Tuesday and Wednesday will put the whole country in condition to be completely swept by a fire. This is liable to do incalculable damage to the stock interests and is a matter that admits of no delay in remedying.
articles.summary: Prairie fires south of Belfield and near Sully Springs; Packard urges fire guards.

articles.text: Bob. Roberts will soon move his saloon into the skating rink. The rink will be re-finished throughout, ceiled, papered, painted and fitted with a glass front.
articles.summary: Bob Roberts will move his saloon into the refitted skating rink.

articles.text: John Munro and the Gifford Bros. are putting up a thousand tons of hay on the Big plateau. This will be the cleanest hay ever put up in this country, as the same ground has been cut over once or twice.
articles.summary: Munro and the Gifford Bros. are putting up 1,000 tons of hay on the Big plateau.

articles.text: Geo. Eckhardt, treasurer of the Milwaukee Brewing Co., who are now operating the large brewery at Bismarck, was in Medora, Monday. He is on his way west and reports trade as opening up well for the new brewery.
articles.summary: Geo. Eckhardt of the Milwaukee Brewing Co. (Bismarck) visited Medora.

articles.text: The wa[y?] Norwegian Abe clawed leather, at the beef camp Monday night, would take the pie in any contest, but he couldn't stay with his name-sake "Crazy." This is the reason he has gone into mourning and not because his love's young dream was blighted.
articles.summary: Norwegian Abe was thrown by a horse named "Crazy" at the beef camp.

articles.text: We know of several cases where pilgrims have come to Dakota with little or no summer clothing, thinking that it would be useless here. The pores of our skin fairly wept at their delusion Tuesday, when we saw the thermometer register 104 in the shade and never crack a smile.
articles.summary: The thermometer reached 104 in the shade Tuesday.

articles.text: Warren Packard, of Warren, Ohio one of the most prominent iron and lumber men in that state and J. J. Fisher, a wealthy young business man of Allentown, Pa., spent the first of the week in Medora and vicinity. They expressed themselves as greatly pleased with their visit, especially at their treatment at the beef camp on Davis creek. As near as they could make out, everything was done according to Hoyle, except that they looked in vain for the piano to accompany the evening lullaby of the cowboys when they were singing the herd to sleep, after having been driven up to the corrall to be milked.
articles.summary: Ohio industrialist Warren Packard and J. J. Fisher of Allentown visited Medora and the Davis Creek beef camp.

articles.text: We neglected in our last issue to mention the Bad Lands minstrel entertainment, given by home talent at the rink, on the evening of the fourth of July. The variety part of the entertainment would have been a complete success if we had brought our guns along and killed all the performers at the beginning of the first act. The orchestra, led by Mose de Spicer, was simply indescribable. To escape a popular uprising, Mose fled the next morning for the Pacific coast. Two other members of the gang, for this or some other reason, skip to-night for the Big Horn country. One of the finest pieces of legerdemain ever witnessed was the invisible way in which the invisible Prof. Wellung deluded a confiding public into believing that there was a professor on the stage who knew the difference between a sleight of hand trick and four dollars a week.
articles.summary: Packard's mock review of the July 4 Bad Lands minstrel show at the rink.

articles.headline: Hotel Arrivals.
articles.text: The following persons registered at the Northern Pacific during the last week: G. P. Williams, Bismarck; M. Wadsworth and wife, B. L. C. Co., Ranch; J. R. Watson, Galesburg, Ill.; E. A. Stedman, Bismarck; Chas. Morey, R quarter circle ranch; George Harmon, Mandan; Wm. G. Cranston, Boston; T. W. Gordon, city; Michael Mullen, Little Missouri; W. M. Kranshaw, Glendive; Dr. A. R. Duncan, Glendive; Warren Packard, Warren, Ohio; John J. Fisher, Allentown, Pa.; Fred Allen, Glendive; James Basch, St. Paul; Dr. H. W. Coe, Mandan; Geo. Auld, Belfield; A. Connell, J. B. Monaghan, Green Bay, Wis.; Gust Noble, Decatur, Ind.; J. W. Buster, Hashknife ranch; S. H. Emerson, C. D. Edick, Bismarck.
articles.summary: Guests registered at the Northern Pacific hotel during the week.

articles.text:
General Store of the N. P. R. C. Co., Medora, Dakota — groceries, dry goods, ready-made clothing, hats, caps, canned goods, harness, saddles, tobacco and cigars, felt shoes, overshoes, boots and shoes, flour and feed; "Hunters Outfits a Specialty"
Brand: Medora Stage & F. Co. — horse brand [Y over cross] on left shoulder; horses strung on stage stations between Medora and Deadwood, Dakota; $25 reward for information on anyone dealing unlawfully with these horses
Northern Pacific Railroad — "The Direct Line Between St. Paul, Minneapolis, or Duluth" and Montana, Idaho, Washington, Oregon, British Columbia, Alaska; Chas. S. Fee, General Passenger Agent, St. Paul
City Drug Store, Medora, Dak., H. M. Jorgens, Proprietor — drugs, patent medicines, perfumery, toilet articles, notions, periodicals, stationery
E. J. Owenhouse, Bozeman, Mont. — stock saddles, Concord harness, bits and spurs, chaparejos, reatas, quirts, hackamores
Minneapolis & St. Louis Ry, "Famous Albert Lea Route" — map ad
articles.summary: Display ads in columns 3-4.

articles.text:
Brand: E. W. Casey, Frank S. Moore, Manager, P.O. Medora, Billings Co., Dak. — KC on left shoulder, F on left hip; 2nd brand same without circle; range O'Donnell creek
Brand: Sloping Bottom Ranch, Lloyd Roberts, Proprietor, P.O. Medora — brand on left hip; range Little Missouri 7 miles south of N. P. R. R.; horse brand same on left shoulder
Brand: Badger Cattle Company, Howard Eaton, M'g'r, P.O. Medora, Billings Co. — VI on left hip, horse brand same; range Beaver creek and Little Missouri river
Brand: Dorr Clark, Spearfish, Dakota — VVV on left side; ear mark under-bit in left ear; range Belle Fourche
Brand: Clark & Plum, Spearfish, Dakota — E6 on left side; ear mark left ear cropped; range Grand river; additional brands ZD, DZ, ZD (bar), circle cross; $100 reward re VVV or E6 ranges
Brand: Little Missouri Horse Company, [?] Tarbell, M'n'g'r, Medora — H on left shoulder; range Davis creek and Little Missouri river
Brand: W. N. Thompson & Co., Wm. Dantz, Manager, P.O. Medora — quarter-circle diamond TD on left hip; vent bar under T. D.; ear mark tip of left ear cut off square
Brand: Lemoyne Cattle Co. (Limited), D. K. Wade, Manager, Medora — LC on left side, reversed C on right hip; range Little Missouri south of the R. R.; ranch Tepee bottom; owners of DW brand
Brand: Soho Cattle Co., Chas. Eaton, Manager, Medora — SO on left side; range Little Missouri river and Beaver creek, north of N. P. R. R.
Brand: Chimney Butte Ranch, Theodore Roosevelt, Proprietor; Ferris & Merrifield, Managers; P.O. Medora — Maltese cross on left hip or right side; down cut dewlap; range six miles south of N. P. R. R. on Little Missouri
Brand: Bullion Creek Horse Ranch, Jack Bullion, Prop., Medora — 55 on left hip; range Bullion creek, twenty miles south of Medora
Brand: N. P. Refrigerator Car Co., Medora — several cattle brands on left side (incl. circle JP and others); also steers purchased of Mason & Lovell; range Little Missouri river and Beaver creek
Brand: Spring Creek Ranch, L. D. & B. Rumsey, J. L. Truscott, Manager, P.O. Medora — circle-R-circle-B on left hip and side; ear marks both ears swallow forked; range south of N. P. R. R. on Little Missouri
Brand: Berry, Boice & Co., P.O. Keith, Montana — 777 on right hip, side and shoulder; range south of N. P. R. R. on Little Missouri river and Beaver creek
Brand: E. G. Paddock, P.O. Medora — six-inch circle-dot on both sides; range six miles north of crossing of N. P. R. R. and Little Missouri; horses four-inch circle-dot on left shoulder and left hip
Brand: Lydia S. Fuller, Frank S. Moore, Manager, P.O. Medora — LSF on left shoulder; range O'Donnell creek
Brand: Custer Trail Cattle Co., A. Alden Eaton, Supt., P.O. Medora — HK in circle on left side; range Little Missouri river, Deep and Davis creeks
Brand: Towers & Gudgell, P.O. Keith, Montana — brand on right side, additional V; range south of N. P. R. R. on Little Missouri river and Beaver creek
Brand: Bad Lands Cattle Co., M. Wadsworth, Manager, P.O. Medora — 71 on right hip and shoulder, bellows, Pd brands; range Little Missouri fifteen miles north of Medora
Brand: Neimmela Ranch, Gregor Lang, Manager, P.O. Medora — thistle and other brands; range Keogh crossing of Little Missouri to Pretty butte
articles.summary: Cattle and horse brand directory.

events.title: Morton County sheriff Geo. Harmon visits Medora
events.summary: Geo. Harmon, sheriff of Morton County, was in Medora.
events.excerpt: Geo. Harmon, sheriff of Morton county, was here last Friday.

events.title: Geo. Auld of Belfield visits Medora
events.summary: Geo. Auld of Belfield was a visitor in Medora.
events.excerpt: Geo. Auld, of Belfield, was a visitor in Medora, Tuesday.

events.date_basis: no date given; week before Thu 16 Jul 1885 issue
events.title: John Warn prospering with new hotel at Glendive
events.summary: John Warn was reported prospering in his new hotel venture at Glendive.
events.excerpt: John Warn seems to be prospering in his new hotel venture at Glendive.

events.title: Charlie Morey plans a dairy near Medora
events.summary: Charlie Morey intended to start a dairy near Medora during the summer.
events.excerpt: Charlie Morey intends starting a dairy near Medora during the summer.

events.title: Dr. Jorgens and family to leave on Cave Hills trip
events.summary: Dr. Jorgens and his family were to start Saturday or Sunday on their trip to the Cave Hills.
events.excerpt: Dr. Jorgens and family will start Saturday or Sunday on their Cave Hills trip.

events.date_basis: no date given; week before Thu 16 Jul 1885 issue
events.title: B. F. Lamb buys 68 head of M bar cattle
events.summary: B. F. Lamb bought sixty-eight head of M bar cattle that the N. P. Refrigerator Car Co. had rounded up.
events.excerpt: B. F. Lamb has bought sixty-eight head of M bar cattle, the N. P. Ref. Car Co. rounded up.

events.date_basis: no date given; week before Thu 16 Jul 1885 issue
events.title: Mrs. Foraier photographs the Bad Lands
events.summary: Mrs. Foraier, an amateur photographer, had taken several good views of the Bad Lands.
events.excerpt: Mrs. Foraier is a successful amateur photographer and has taken several good views of the Bad Lands.

events.date_basis: no date given; week before Thu 16 Jul 1885 issue
events.title: B. Bar becomes Kansas City purchasing agent for Rogers & Rogers
events.summary: B. Bar was located at Kansas City as purchasing agent for Rogers & Rogers, live stock commission merchants.
events.excerpt: B. Bar is located at Kansas City as purchasing agent for Rogers & Rogers, Live Stock commission merchants.

events.title: Mrs. Malloy opens her new hotel on Main Street
events.summary: Mrs. Malloy moved from the Western house to her new building on Main Street, and supper was served at the new hotel that evening.
events.excerpt: Mrs. Malloy moved yesterday from the Western house, to her new building on Main street. Supper was served at the new hotel last evening.

events.title: Aleck Connell buys outfit to start a Bad Lands ranch
events.summary: Aleck Connell, Ford's freighting partner the previous summer, bought teams and an outfit in Medora and planned to take up a ranch in the Bad Lands and stock it with cattle.
events.excerpt: He intends taking up a ranch in the Bad Lands and stocking it with cattle.

events.title: Medora post office begins selling money orders
events.summary: Beginning that day, domestic and foreign money orders were sold at the Medora post office.
events.excerpt: Beginning with to-day, money orders, both domestic and foreign, will be sold at the Medora office.

events.title: Dr. Duncan of Glendive splints Joe McCoul's leg
events.summary: Dr. Duncan of Glendive was in Medora and put a plaster-of-paris splint on Joe McCoul's leg.
events.excerpt: He put a plaster-of-paris splint on Joe. McCoul's leg

events.title: Rassie Deffebach moves family to Dickinson, takes charge of Bad Lands Cattle Co. ranch
events.summary: Rassie Deffebach returned from Dickinson, where his family was settled; he was to be at the Bad Lands Cattle Co.'s ranch handling that outfit.
events.excerpt: He will be at the Bad Lands cattle Co's. ranch and handle that outfit.

events.title: Legislator Dr. H. W. Coe in Medora closing up census work
events.summary: Dr. H. W. Coe of Mandan, the district's member of the legislature, was in Medora closing up Coll McClellan's census work.
events.excerpt: Dr. H. W. Coe, of Mandan, our member of the legislature, was here Monday closing up Coll McClellan's census work.

events.title: The Marquise de Morès leaves on Big Horn hunting trip
events.summary: The Marquise, Wm. Van Driesche and a hunting party of Vic and Frank Smith, Tom Skinner and Sweet were to start that evening for Huntley, Mont., the starting point for an overland trip to the Big Horn; they expected to be gone about a month.
events.excerpt: The Marquise, Wm. Van Driesche and hunting party consisting of Vic and Frank Smith, Tom Skinner and Sweet start this evening for Huntley, Mont.

events.title: A. R. Kelsey of J. S. Collins & Co. calls at the Cow Boy office
events.summary: A. R. Kelsey, manager of the Glendive branch of J. S. Collins & Co., called at the Cow Boy office and reported good trade.
events.excerpt: A. R. Kelsey, manager of the Glendive branch of J. S. Collins & Co., called at the Cow Boy office this morning.

events.date_basis: "on or about August 10", reported Thu 16 Jul 1885
events.title: J. S. Collins & Co. to move Glendive branch to Miles City
events.summary: J. S. Collins & Co. planned to move its Glendive branch to Miles City on or about August 10, where the firm was building a brick store room.
events.excerpt: the branch will be removed there on or about August 10. The firm is now building a brick store room for their accommodation in Miles.

events.title: Range beef not yet first-class
events.summary: The Cow Boy reported that beef slaughtered at Medora had not met expectations because the grass had grown to quantity, not quality, and doubted first-class beef would be killed before August 1.
events.excerpt: It is doubtful if any first-class beef will be killed before August 1.

events.title: Prairie fire burns in the Bad Lands near Sully Springs
events.summary: A large part of the country south of Belfield had been burned over, and a prairie fire was burning in the Bad Lands near Sully Springs; no fire guards had been made.
events.excerpt: yesterday one was burning in the Bad Lands near Sully Springs.

events.date_basis: weather record for week ending July 15, Thu 16 Jul 1885
events.title: Hot, dry week; noon temperature reaches 110
events.summary: T. Martin's weather record for the week ending July 15 showed a high of 110 degrees at noon on July 14 and no rainfall recorded.
events.excerpt: At 12 o'clock m., July 14....110 degs.

events.title: Thermometer registers 104 in the shade
events.summary: The thermometer registered 104 in the shade on Tuesday.
events.excerpt: we saw the thermometer register 104 in the shade and never crack a smile.

events.date_basis: no date given; week before Thu 16 Jul 1885 issue
events.title: Mose Ryder in charge of Cannon Ball beef herd
events.summary: Mose Ryder had charge of the Cannon Ball beef herd, where Hashknife cattle unfit for slaughter were being grazed.
events.excerpt: Mose Ryder has charge of the Cannon Ball beef herd

events.title: Last Hashknife bunch held on the divide until August
events.summary: The last bunch of Hashknife cattle, due to be delivered the day before, was being held on the divide and would not be brought in before August 1.
events.excerpt: will not be brought in before the first of August.

events.title: Bob Roberts to move saloon into the skating rink
events.summary: Bob Roberts planned to move his saloon into the skating rink, which would be refinished, ceiled, papered, painted and fitted with a glass front.
events.excerpt: Bob. Roberts will soon move his saloon into the skating rink.

events.date_basis: no date given; week before Thu 16 Jul 1885 issue
events.title: Munro and Gifford Bros. putting up 1,000 tons of hay
events.summary: John Munro and the Gifford Bros. were putting up a thousand tons of hay on the Big plateau.
events.excerpt: John Munro and the Gifford Bros. are putting up a thousand tons of hay on the Big plateau.

events.title: Milwaukee Brewing Co. treasurer Geo. Eckhardt in Medora
events.summary: Geo. Eckhardt, treasurer of the Milwaukee Brewing Co., operating the large brewery at Bismarck, was in Medora on his way west.
events.excerpt: was in Medora, Monday. He is on his way west and reports trade as opening up well for the new brewery.

events.title: Norwegian Abe thrown at the beef camp
events.summary: At the beef camp, Norwegian Abe 'clawed leather' but couldn't stay on his namesake horse "Crazy."
events.excerpt: he couldn't stay with his name-sake "Crazy."

events.date_basis: "the first of the week" before Thu 16 Jul 1885
events.title: Warren Packard and J. J. Fisher visit Medora and Davis Creek beef camp
events.summary: Warren Packard of Warren, Ohio, and J. J. Fisher of Allentown, Pa., spent the first of the week in Medora and vicinity and were pleased with their treatment at the beef camp on Davis Creek.
events.excerpt: spent the first of the week in Medora and vicinity.

events.date_basis: "evening of the fourth of July", reported Thu 16 Jul 1885
events.title: Bad Lands minstrel entertainment at the rink
events.summary: A home-talent minstrel entertainment was given at the rink on the evening of July 4; the paper lampooned the performers, the orchestra led by Mose de Spicer and Prof. Wellung's sleight of hand.
events.excerpt: the Bad Lands minstrel entertainment, given by home talent at the rink, on the evening of the fourth of July.

events.date_basis: no date given; week before Thu 16 Jul 1885 issue
events.title: M. Wadsworth and wife among Northern Pacific hotel guests
events.summary: Guests at the Northern Pacific hotel during the week included M. Wadsworth and wife of the B. L. C. Co. ranch, J. W. Buster of the Hashknife ranch, and visitors from Bismarck, Glendive, Boston, St. Paul and elsewhere.
events.excerpt: M. Wadsworth and wife, B. L. C. Co., Ranch

events.date_basis: standing brand ad in Thu 16 Jul 1885 issue
events.title: Chimney Butte Ranch brand ad lists Theodore Roosevelt as proprietor
events.summary: The brand column carried the Chimney Butte Ranch ad: Theodore Roosevelt, proprietor; Ferris & Merrifield, managers; Maltese cross brand, range six miles south of the N. P. R. R. on the Little Missouri.
events.excerpt: Theodore Roosevelt, Proprietor. Ferris & Merrifield, Managers.

events.title: Agent reports no danger at Cheyenne and Arapahoe agencies
events.summary: Special agent Armstrong telegraphed from Fort Reno that there was no danger of trouble at the Arapahoe and Cheyenne agencies.
events.excerpt: there was no danger of trouble arising at the Arapahoe and Cheyenne agencies.

events.date_basis: no date given; week before Thu 16 Jul 1885 issue
events.title: Texas trail drivers arrested under Kansas quarantine law
events.summary: Trail drivers including J. R. Blocker and J. W. Driskill were arrested by a deputy U.S. marshal and taken to Dodge City, with over 50,000 head stopped south of the Canadian River.
events.excerpt: have been arrested by deputy U. S. Marshal Bell and taken to Dodge City, Kansas.
